beats.label: S1 · Nanny for a doll
beats.text: Leanne arrives to care for baby Jericho, a reborn doll Dorothy treats as real to survive her son's crib death. Sean, alone in his grief, plays along.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the household's central lie and the arrangement Leanne walks into — the premise every later shock depends on.

beats.label: S1 · A real baby in the crib
beats.text: Days later, a living infant appears in the crib in the doll's place. Dorothy behaves as if Jericho never died; Sean can't remove the baby or explain how he arrived.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the show's engine — the impossible baby whose origin drives every investigation for three seasons.

beats.label: S1 · Leanne is not Leanne
beats.text: Julian's investigation finds the real Leanne Grayson died in a 2007 Wisconsin house fire. He treats the nanny as an imposter running a con on the family.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the fault line that runs the rest of the series: is Leanne a scam or something else entirely.

beats.label: S1 · Uncle George at the door
beats.text: Leanne's unnerving uncle George arrives demanding she leave with him. Sean and Julian now suspect she belongs to something older and stranger than a scam.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First appearance of the cult through its emissary — George is the recurring pressure on Leanne through S4.

beats.label: S1 · How Jericho actually died
beats.text: Flashbacks reveal Dorothy, sleep-deprived and alone, forgot the baby in a hot car; she then tended his corpse in catatonia for four days until Julian found her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The trauma the whole show orbits, and the secret Sean and Julian will spend seasons keeping from Dorothy.

beats.label: S1 · May Markham surfaces
beats.text: At Jericho's baptism, Dorothy identifies George's companion as May Markham, leader of a cult supposedly burned to death years earlier.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the Church of the Lesser Saints and reframes the story from domestic mystery to cult siege.

beats.label: S1 · Leanne leaves, doll returns
beats.text: Cult members appear on the street and spirit Leanne away; upstairs, the living Jericho is once again a reborn doll, which Dorothy finally drops.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The exact state the household is in as S2 opens: baby gone, doll back, Dorothy about to start screaming for her son.

cliffhanger.text: The living Jericho vanishes with Leanne into a cult everyone thought was dead. Dorothy has just accepted that her son is a doll, but not that he is gone.
questions: Where has the real baby been taken, and whose child is he?
What does the Church of the Lesser Saints actually want with the Turners?
Will Sean ever tell Dorothy that her real son died months ago in the car?

characters.name: Dorothy Turner
characters.line: Philadelphia TV reporter whose psychotic break lets her treat a reborn doll as her infant son; still has no idea Jericho died in her care.

characters.name: Sean Turner
characters.line: Dorothy's chef husband, quietly grieving; plagued by unexplained splinters and losing his senses since Leanne arrived.

characters.name: Julian
characters.line: Dorothy's sardonic younger brother and one of the few who know Jericho died; drives the investigation into Leanne.

characters.name: Leanne Grayson
characters.line: The devout eighteen-year-old 'nanny' — an identity that belongs to a girl dead since 2007, and the conduit through which a living baby appeared in the crib.

characters.name: Uncle George
characters.line: Leanne's unsettling relative and the cult's ambassador; came to bring her home and left with a warning that his wife would return for her.

characters.name: May Markham
characters.line: Leader of the Church of the Lesser Saints, believed killed in an ATF fire years ago and now walking around Philadelphia collecting Leanne.

characters.name: Natalie
characters.line: Dorothy's kinesiologist friend who prescribed the reborn doll therapy and now knows a real baby was in the house.

characters.name: Tobe
characters.line: Sean's sous chef, sweetly infatuated with Leanne and oblivious to the household's secret.

beats.label: S2 · Dorothy calls the cops
beats.text: Dorothy reports Jericho's 'kidnapping' to police; Sean and Julian cover with a story that the doll therapy broke her mind, hiding that a real baby was ever there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames the whole season — Dorothy is fighting for a baby everyone else has to pretend was never there.

beats.label: S2 · The pizza trap
beats.text: Dorothy chases every lead to Leanne. A pizza-delivery ruse locates her at a mansion caretaking role; Dorothy has Tobe drug the pizza and bring her home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Dorothy stops being reactive — she is the one who captures Leanne, flipping the power dynamic that opens the back half.

beats.label: S2 · Attic and sinkhole
beats.text: Dorothy locks Leanne in the attic and interrogates her nightly. When Leanne escapes, Dorothy buries her in the new basement sinkhole; Sean digs her out, appalled.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows how far Dorothy will go and cracks Sean's alignment with her — the fissure Leanne will exploit for the rest of the season.

beats.label: S2 · George's ransom bargain
beats.text: A fake ransom lures Uncle George back to the house. He offers to heal Sean and return Jericho — but only if Leanne is handed to the cult for 'purification.'
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the terms of the war: the cult wants Leanne back to kill her, and it's willing to trade the baby to get her.

beats.label: S2 · Leanne turns on George
beats.text: Leanne warns Sean that George is lying. She defies him, sleeps with Julian, and hints someone worse than May is coming; a rattled George is hit by a car outside.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Leanne actively picks a side against the cult and forms the Julian bond that carries into S3.

beats.label: S2 · Josephine's purification
beats.text: Aunt Josephine arrives and locks Leanne in the attic to 'purify' her. Dorothy interrupts with a shovel; Leanne finishes Josephine off with a red-hot dagger.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First on-screen kill of a cult elder and the first hint that Leanne is more than a runaway — the burnt body stays hidden in the walls.

beats.label: S2 · Jericho returned
beats.text: A living Jericho appears in the nursery, cradled by Leanne, who declares the Turners her family and privately vows war on the Church.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Season closes with Leanne installed as protector-in-residence and openly at war with the cult — the exact setup S3 opens on.

cliffhanger.text: Leanne has bought her way into the family with a living child and a body hidden in the basement. She is no longer a captive — she is the Turners' protector, and alone in her room she has vowed war on the Church.
questions: What is Leanne actually capable of, and where does this second Jericho come from?
How will the Church of the Lesser Saints answer her declaration?
Can Sean and Julian ever tell Dorothy that her real son died in the car?

characters.name: Dorothy Turner
characters.line: Convinced her baby was kidnapped by the cult; ruthless in pursuit of him and completely unaware she caused his death last summer.

characters.name: Sean Turner
characters.line: Wavering between Dorothy and Leanne; his senses have returned and he is quietly moving from atheism to prayer.

characters.name: Julian
characters.line: Dorothy's brother, running interference for both women; slept with Leanne during the Christmas week and won't stop thinking about it.

characters.name: Leanne Grayson
characters.line: No longer a captive — the household's live-in protector, who killed a cult elder and produced a living baby to buy her place.

characters.name: Uncle George
characters.line: Cult emissary rebuffed by the Turners and hit by a car outside the house; his current whereabouts are unclear.

characters.name: Aunt Josephine
characters.line: Higher-ranked cult figure sent to ritually 'purify' Leanne; killed with a fiery dagger and burned in the basement.

characters.name: Officer Stephanie Reyes
characters.line: First responder from the day Jericho died, now assigned to the 'kidnapping'; visibly skeptical of the Turners' cover story.

characters.name: Tobe
characters.line: Sean's sous chef, unknowingly delivered the drugged pizza that captured Leanne; still smitten with her.

beats.label: S3 · Paranoid Leanne
beats.text: Three months later, Leanne is paranoid and won't leave the house. An intruder ransacks the bedroom while the Turners are at the beach and steals her ritual dagger.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the season's baseline — Leanne under siege, and puts the dagger in cult hands where it will keep resurfacing.

beats.label: S3 · Jericho isn't hers
beats.text: Julian secretly runs DNA on Jericho and confirms the baby is not Dorothy's biological son. Dorothy refuses to believe him; the truth stays trapped.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First concrete proof the miracle baby is a substitute, seeding the S4 revelation that he belongs to someone else entirely.

beats.label: S3 · Leanne's followers
beats.text: Runaways from the Church of the Lesser Saints camp in the park and worship Leanne as a rebel who broke free. Two cult members attack her at a block party.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The cult splits: Leanne now has her own disciples, and the mainline Church escalates to physical assault.

beats.label: S3 · Sean turns to God
beats.text: Sean turns devout and invites his pastor Nancy over. Dorothy realises she has no memory of Sean ever leaving for a cooking show; Sean and Julian gaslight her through it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sean picks Leanne over Dorothy's sanity — the alliance that makes Dorothy the household's dissident.

beats.label: S3 · Jericho on a string
beats.text: When Dorothy tries to send her away, Leanne makes Jericho briefly vanish, proving the baby is her gift and can be revoked. Sean forces Dorothy to let her stay.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Leanne stops pretending — she is openly using the child as leverage, and the family folds.

beats.label: S3 · Isabelle on live TV
beats.text: Reporter Isabelle pieces together the truth and confronts Dorothy. On live TV she is killed by a stray bullet at a police standoff; Leanne smiles as she watches.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First strong hint Leanne can reach out and touch her enemies at a distance — the outside world is no longer safe from her.

beats.label: S3 · Dorothy falls
beats.text: Frank brings a psychiatrist who evaluates Dorothy instead of Leanne. Dorothy tries to flee with Jericho, and the rotting banister collapses, dropping her to the floor below.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the season with Dorothy broken at Leanne's feet — the precise physical state and power balance S4 opens on.

cliffhanger.text: Dorothy lies broken at the foot of the stairs, looking up at Leanne cradling Jericho. Leanne is no longer hiding what she can do; she runs the house, and the family knows it.
questions: How badly is Dorothy hurt, and does she remember Leanne let her fall?
What is Leanne willing to do to the Turners to keep them as her family?
How will the Church answer the fact that she is now openly powerful?

characters.name: Leanne Grayson
characters.line: Openly supernatural, using Jericho as leverage over Dorothy; hunted by the Church and revered by its defectors in the park.

characters.name: Dorothy Turner
characters.line: Paralyzed at the foot of the stairs after Leanne let her fall; still doesn't know her real son died last summer.

characters.name: Sean Turner
characters.line: Devout now, siding with Leanne to keep the child; actively gaslighting Dorothy about his missing weeks on the cooking show.

characters.name: Julian
characters.line: Sober, dating Veera, still sleeping with Leanne; proved Jericho isn't Dorothy's biologically and no one will act on it.

characters.name: Jericho
characters.line: The living toddler installed by Leanne — DNA-confirmed as not Dorothy's biological son.

characters.name: Uncle George
characters.line: Alive and recovered, conferring with Roscoe outside the Turner house and calling it 'rotting.'

characters.name: Isabelle
characters.line: Dorothy's rival reporter who worked out the Jericho lie; killed on live TV by a stray bullet before she could publish.

characters.name: Frank
characters.line: Dorothy's father, covertly sent a psychiatrist to evaluate Dorothy under the guise of evaluating Leanne, and instead handed Leanne authority over Dorothy's care.

beats.label: S4 · Pigeons in the driveway
beats.text: Dorothy comes home paraplegic and refuses Leanne's help. Cult members ambush Leanne in the driveway; a flock of pigeons descends and drives them off.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First unambiguous supernatural display — Leanne now commands the natural world, and Dorothy has locked her out of the family.

beats.label: S4 · Bobbie's séance
beats.text: Dorothy hires nurses Beverly and Bobbie to keep Leanne away. Bobbie, a medium, holds a séance during which she hears a baby crying that no one else can find.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Independent confirmation that the real Jericho's spirit is still nearby — the moral stakes of the whole show, restated by a stranger.

beats.label: S4 · Neighbors and sinkhole
beats.text: The Turners realise the Church has moved cult members onto the block. When they throw a party to smoke them out, Leanne opens a sinkhole in the street with her mind.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The war goes public. Leanne demonstrates telekinetic power in front of witnesses; Sean starts to be genuinely afraid of her.

beats.label: S4 · George's mundane truth
beats.text: George tells Sean and Julian that Leanne is no fallen angel — just a stalker who fixated on Dorothy in 2011, drugged Sean, and passed off a dead addict's baby as Jericho.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The alternative explanation the men choose to believe — and the reason they agree to hand Leanne over.

beats.label: S4 · The handoff, reversed
beats.text: Sean and Julian bind Leanne and hand her to George for purification. Leanne kills George with his own fiery dagger and completes the ritual on him instead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Point of no return: the men betray Leanne, Leanne butchers the cult single-handed, and any pretence of a shared household ends.

beats.label: S4 · Dorothy remembers
beats.text: Julian plays Dorothy the voicemail from the day Jericho died and she finally remembers leaving him in the car. Leanne offers Dorothy a life with just her and the baby.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's central secret is finally spoken to the person it belongs to — everything after this is Dorothy's choice.

beats.label: S4 · Fire
beats.text: Dorothy refuses; there is no baby in the house. Leanne burns the house down and steps into the flames. Reyes tells Julian that the cult resurrected him too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the series: Leanne walks into her own pyre and the survivors learn the cult's reach was wider than Leanne alone.

cliffhanger.text: The Turners walk out of the burnt house without Leanne and without a child. Reyes tells Julian the Church saved his life last Christmas for a reason it hasn't named.
questions: Is Leanne truly dead, or has she returned to whatever she came from?
What does the Church expect Julian to do with the life it gave back to him?
Can Dorothy and Sean live with what they now remember about the day Jericho died?

characters.name: Leanne Grayson
characters.line: Openly wielding supernatural power and convinced God has abandoned her; walked into a fire she set after Dorothy refused her as a daughter.

characters.name: Dorothy Turner
characters.line: Paraplegic and, at last, remembering that her real son died in her care last summer; refused Leanne's offer of a substitute family.

characters.name: Sean Turner
characters.line: Turned on Leanne after her true nature surfaced; stabbed himself during the failed handoff and finished the season out of the burnt house.

characters.name: Julian
characters.line: Helped Sean betray Leanne; ends the season told by Reyes that the cult was the one who brought him back from the overdose last Christmas.

characters.name: Uncle George
characters.line: Cult leader who ran the purification ritual on Leanne himself; killed by her with his own fiery dagger.

characters.name: Officer Stephanie Reyes
characters.line: Revealed as a cult 'chosen sister,' resurrected as a teenager and assigned to watch Leanne the whole time.

characters.name: Bobbie (Roberta)
characters.line: Dorothy's medium nurse whose séance confirmed a real Jericho was crying somewhere no one could reach.

characters.name: Beverly
characters.line: Dorothy's other live-in nurse; dead of a snakebite at the zoo party according to George's account.
